# 1 Enoch Chapter 55 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**1** After this I saw another army — men in chariots riding on the wind. They came from the east and swept toward the west.

**2** I heard those chariots before I could fully see them — a roar and a rumble, countless numbers, pouring into a valley like a flood.

**3** That day I watched a great trembling overtake heaven itself. The entire host of the Most High — the angels, millions upon millions — were shaken with violent agitation.

**4** The Head of Days was seated on his throne of glory, with angels and righteous ones standing in attendance all around him.

**5** A terrible trembling seized me. Fear locked its grip on me, my legs buckled, my spirit drained away, and I collapsed face-down on the ground.

**6** Michael dispatched one of the holy angels to lift me up. When he raised me, my spirit came back to me — I simply had not been able to bear the sight of that vast host, or the convulsions and shaking of heaven.

**7** Michael said to me: "Why has this vision shaken you so completely? Today is still the day of his mercy. He has been patient and compassionate toward those who live on earth.

**8** But the day is coming — the day of his power, his punishment, his reckoning — a day the Lord of Spirits has readied for all who refuse to bow before righteous law, who deny righteous judgment, who use his name carelessly. That day is set: for the chosen it means covenant-security; for sinners it means full inquisition."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering aimed at modern readability. Michael's speech (vv. 7–8) provides the theological framework for the entire judgment sequence. The 'day of mercy' versus 'day of judgment' is central to the Parables' theodicy.*
